clue.text: It's marvellous to be put in a carriage with courtesy

indicators.note: something put in a vehicle is placed inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a fly is a light one-horse hired carriage of the nineteenth century, kept with its article
'It's fab!' is slang for 'it's marvellous'

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled to be handed politely into a coach.
explanation.walkthrough: A fly was a light horse-drawn cab, not an insect, and fab is sixties slang for marvellous.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting affably means behaving in a friendly, gracious manner, which is a courteous way to behave.

clue.text: Consequences of following a dull husband

parts.note: after means following in time
mat, or matt, describes a dull surface without shine
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: What comes of trailing after a boring spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: An aftermath is the period of results following an event, especially an unpleasant one, so it means its effects.

clue.text: Part of the Yard's guard for criminal

parts.note: a foot is one third of a yard
a pad is a protective guard, as worn in cricket

explanation.surface: A division of Scotland Yard guarding against a villain.
explanation.walkthrough: The Yard suggests Scotland Yard, London's police; here it is the unit of length.
explanation.definitionFit: A footpad was a robber who attacked travellers on foot, an old word for a street criminal.

clue.text: Shelled head of republic

parts.note: surface reading: a president who has been bombarded with shells
setter's reading: head is slang for nut, and the republic is a large South American country, so a nut in its shell

explanation.walkthrough: Shelled means having a shell, not shot at, and head is the slang sense nut.
explanation.definitionFit: This large edible seed grows in a hard shell in the South American rainforest, so it is that country's nut.

clue.text: You will no longer shout like this

wordplay.note: the old contraction of 'ye will', with ye the archaic plural of you, a form no longer in use; drop its apostrophe

explanation.surface: A promise that someone will stop raising their voice.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue says how people no longer say 'you will': as ye'll, which without its apostrophe is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To yell is to cry out loudly, so it is a synonym for shout.

clue.text: Communicated with various dailies

indicators.note: various suggests the letters come in assorted arrangements, so they are reordered

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone kept in touch with several daily newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: To liaise is to keep in contact and cooperate with another party, so the past tense matches communicated.

clue.text: No profit on article like this

definitions.text: No profit on article like this

parts.note: making no profit means running at a loss
a leader is a newspaper's main editorial article

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper's remark about an item sold without making money.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a shop sells this kind of item at no profit to draw customers in.
explanation.definitionFit: A loss leader is a product sold below cost to attract shoppers who then buy other things.

clue.text: Leaders of African country, coastal republic, are found here

definitions.text: Leaders of African country, coastal republic, are found here

indicators.note: leaders are those at the front, so only the opening letters count

parts.note: the opening letters of the five words

explanation.surface: The rulers of a West African coastal state are based in its capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer: Accra is the capital of Ghana, a coastal republic in Africa, where its leaders sit.
explanation.definitionFit: Accra is the seat of government of Ghana on the Atlantic coast, where national leaders are based.

clue.text: Nightingale's base a rustic disturbed

indicators.note: something disturbed is knocked out of place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A countryman disturbs a songbird at its roost.
explanation.walkthrough: The Nightingale is Florence Nightingale, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Florence Nightingale ran her famous military hospital at Scutari, near Constantinople, during the Crimean War.

clue.text: Old copper on beat soundly stayed in place

parts.note: D stood for the old penny, a copper coin
to welt is to thrash, beat hard

explanation.surface: A former policeman walking his patrol stayed put.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper and beat call up a policeman on patrol; the copper is a coin, and soundly means thoroughly here.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell is to live or remain somewhere, so the past tense means remained in one place.

clue.text: Thunderer article names girl

parts.note: Thor is the Norse god of thunder
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: The Times newspaper (nicknamed the Thunderer) runs a piece naming a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: The Thunderer is the old nickname of The Times itself, but here it is the Norse god.
explanation.definitionFit: Thora is a female first name, and crosswords often use girl to clue such names.

clue.text: Oxford inhabitant osculates wildly

indicators.note: doing something wildly means doing it without order, so the letters are thrown about

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written; to osculate is to kiss

explanation.surface: An Oxford resident kisses with abandon.
explanation.walkthrough: Matthew Arnold called Oxford the 'home of lost causes', so a hopeless cause lives there.
explanation.definitionFit: Arnold's famous phrase describes the university town as home to hopeless campaigns, making such a cause a resident.

clue.text: Two engineers put things right

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
a pair is two of something

explanation.surface: A couple of engineers come to fix things.
explanation.walkthrough: The engineers come first in the answer, then the two.
explanation.definitionFit: To repair is to mend or fix what is broken, restoring it to working order.

clue.text: Lear was known to be so agreeable

parts.words: Lear was known to be so
parts.note: surface reading: King Lear's reputation, a tragic and difficult monarch

parts.words: Lear was known to be so
parts.note: setter's reading: Edward Lear wrote 'How ... to know Mr Lear!', describing himself as nice to know

explanation.surface: A remark on what Lear was reputed to be like.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lear is Edward Lear, the nonsense poet, whose self-portrait poem opens 'How pleasant to know Mr Lear!'
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasant means agreeable, nice, enjoyable company, which is how the poem describes its author.

clue.text: Unfair? Baseball certainly is!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the idiom for unsporting behaviour
second meaning: literally, baseball is a different bat-and-ball game from the English one

explanation.walkthrough: The British idiom for something dishonourable is literally true of baseball, which is a different sport.
explanation.definitionFit: In British English, saying something isn't the done thing in sport means it is unsporting or unjust.

clue.text: A university's beginning to study this poet

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter only

parts.note: the opening letter of university
a den is a private room for working, a study

explanation.surface: A university starting a course on a particular poet.
explanation.walkthrough: W H Auden was an Anglo-American poet of the twentieth century.
explanation.definitionFit: W H Auden wrote 'Funeral Blues' and many other poems, so he is a famous example of a poet.

clue.text: Places for praying., or a political group

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the Tories are Britain's Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A choice between chapels and a political party.
explanation.definitionFit: An oratory is a small chapel or room set aside for private worship and prayer.

clue.text: Start term in a slack period

parts.note: as in 'they're off', at the start of a race
a season is a period, a term

explanation.surface: Beginning a school term during a quiet time.
explanation.definitionFit: The off-season is the quiet part of the year when business, tourism or sport is less active.

clue.text: Had seat in Poplar, say? Useful for the cabinet

parts.note: sat in means had a seat in
poplar is one kind of timber; say marks an example

explanation.surface: An MP sat for the London seat of Poplar, a possible cabinet minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Poplar is a district of East London and seat and cabinet suggest Parliament, but the cabinet is furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Satinwood is a glossy hardwood prized by furniture makers for fine cabinets and veneers.

clue.text: No unseen cause for  this anguish?

parts.words: No unseen cause for  this anguish?
parts.note: surface reading: a puzzle about distress with no hidden reason

parts.words: No unseen cause for  this anguish?
parts.note: setter's reading: the proverb 'what the eye doesn't see, the heart doesn't grieve over'

explanation.walkthrough: By the proverb, what is never seen cannot make the heart grieve, so no unseen thing causes this pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartache is emotional suffering or grief, a deep sorrow that matches anguish.

clue.text: Amnesty initially frees older: relatives

indicators.note: initially points to the very first letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter of amnesty
to untie someone is to free them

explanation.surface: A human rights group frees older prisoners.
explanation.definitionFit: Aunts are relatives of an older generation, and the affectionate plural names them.

clue.text: Scrap producing dust up in mill

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a scrap is a brawl
second meaning: mill is old slang for a boxing bout, and a dust-up is a brawl

explanation.surface: Waste material creating dust in a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: Scrap and mill look industrial, but a scrap is a brawl and a mill is a prize fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A fight is a physical struggle or brawl, which both informal words describe.

clue.text: Astronomer one spotted in unnamed sailing-ship

indicators.note: something spotted in a place is seen within it, so it sits inside
unnamed means without a name, and N is the abbreviation for name, so that letter goes

parts.note: a galleon is a large old sailing ship
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A stargazer spots someone aboard a mystery ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove N from GALLEON, then put I between the Ls.
explanation.definitionFit: Galileo was the Italian scientist whose telescope revealed Jupiter's moons, a famous stargazer.

clue.text: It might well be called an outstanding talent

parts.note: surface reading: something likely to be described as a gift
setter's reading: in bridge you bid, or call, the suit in which you hold many cards

explanation.surface: Something that might be described as a remarkable gift.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, a player holding many cards of one suit often calls (bids) it; figuratively, that suit is a strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's long suit is the thing they are especially good at, their strong point.

clue.text: One who weeps, when beaten?

parts.note: surface reading: someone who cries after a beating
setter's reading: the playground rhyme 'finders keepers, ... weepers', about the defeated party

explanation.walkthrough: Beaten means defeated in a game, and the rhyme says the one who lost is the one who weeps.
explanation.definitionFit: A loser is the person defeated in a contest, the one beaten by the winner.

clue.text: Import substance

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the import of a statement is its meaning
second meaning: the substance of an argument is its gist

explanation.walkthrough: Import looks like trade goods brought in, but here it is the noun for meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words can mean the meaning or gist of something said or written.

clue.text: Include Li in capital for another

indicators.note: to include is to take in, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: Bern is the capital of Switzerland
taken as written; Li is the symbol for lithium

explanation.surface: An instruction to put something into a capital city to make a different one.
explanation.walkthrough: BER(LI)N: the Swiss capital takes in the two letters to make the German one.
explanation.definitionFit: Berlin is the German capital city, so it is another capital besides Bern.

clue.text: Lightweight tot

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a small unit of weight, a sixteenth of an ounce
second meaning: a small drink of spirits

explanation.walkthrough: Lightweight and tot suggest a small child, but one is a unit of weight and the other a nip of whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a tiny avoirdupois measure and a small glass of liquor.

clue.text: Lure a king inside for a sail

indicators.note: inside places one piece within the walls of the other

parts.note: a spinner is a revolving fishing lure
taken as written
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Tempting a monarch indoors to go sailing.
explanation.walkthrough: Lure looks like a verb, but it is the noun: a spinner is a fishing lure that revolves in the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinnaker is a large three-cornered sail set at the front of a yacht running before the wind.

clue.text: Colossal volley, or part of it

indicators.note: part of it says the answer is a section of the words just given

parts.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A huge burst of gunfire, or a share of one.
explanation.walkthrough: Volley serves twice: as the definition and as part of the string that holds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo is a simultaneous discharge of guns, which is exactly what a volley of fire is.

clue.text: Put out stories showing extreme optimism

indicators.note: something put out is disturbed or disordered, so the letters lose their order

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Publishing tales that look on the bright side.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosy outlook is a hopeful one, so the superlative describes the most hopeful view possible.

clue.text: Soldier poet's courage

parts.note: a man is a private soldier, as in officers and men
Thomas Hood was a nineteenth-century English poet

explanation.surface: The bravery of a war poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Manhood can mean manly qualities such as bravery and spirit, so it serves as a synonym for valour.
